name: Eldad and Medad
charge: Prophesying in the camp when the spirit rested on them, and being defended by Moses
summary: Seventy elders were gathered to the tabernacle to be given of the spirit that was on Moses. Two of the written men stayed in the camp, and the spirit rested on them there, and they prophesied. A young man ran and told Moses, and Joshua said, My lord Moses, forbid them. Moses answered, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord's people were prophets.
offense: They were of the written number but they were not at the tent. Nothing in the account says they refused to go, and the record does not accuse them; what it records is that the spirit rested on them where they were (Numbers 11:25), and that they did not conceal it or wait for permission before speaking. The complaint against them came from the camp and from Moses' own servant (Numbers 11:27), and the two men are not shown answering it.
judgment: Moses refused to silence them and turned the rebuke on the man who wanted it done: enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord's people were prophets (Numbers 11:29), and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them. The case is entered because the blessing was defended by the one person whose standing it might have threatened, and because the wish Moses expressed is the thing Joel later prophesies and Peter cites at Pentecost as fulfilled. Two men who were not in the room are the volume's earliest evidence that the gift is not confined to the appointed place.

verses.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, Gather unto me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom thou knowest to be the elders of the people, and officers over them; and bring them unto the tabernacle of the congregation, that they may stand there with thee.

And I will come down and talk with thee there: and I will take of the spirit which is upon thee, and will put it upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with thee, that thou bear it not thyself alone.
And Moses went out, and told the people the words of the Lord, and gathered the seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them round about the tabernacle.

And the Lord came down in a cloud, and spake unto him, and took of the spirit that was upon him, and gave it unto the seventy elders: and it came to pass, that, when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease.

But there remained two of the men in the camp, the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the spirit rested upon them; and they were of them that were written, but went not out unto the tabernacle: and they prophesied in the camp.
And there ran a young man, and told Moses, and said, Eldad and Medad do prophesy in the camp.
And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses, one of his young men, answered and said, My lord Moses, forbid them.
And Moses said unto him, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord’s people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them!

text.text: But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel;

And it shall come to pass in the last days, saith God, I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams:
And on my servants and on my handmaidens I will pour out in those days of my Spirit; and they shall prophesy:

entries.commentary: The Most High hates it when His people complain. He had just destroyed Egypt for Israel, its land, its infrastructure, its firstborn, and drowned its army in the sea, all to save the people out; then on the other side of the wilderness, at the first trial or tribulation, the people jumped off His bandwagon, and the same is still being done to this day. The Lord heard the complaining, and His anger was kindled, and the fire of the Lord burnt among them. Vengeance, when it punisheth, does not pass by him that speaketh unrighteous things; the murmurer receives the vengeance of the Lord. Nothing spoken behind closed doors is hidden. Inquisition is made into the counsels of the ungodly, by the Lord and His angels, the same council seen when the Lord asked who shall persuade Ahab that he may fall at Ramothgilead; the sound of a man's words comes unto the Lord, for the ear of jealousy heareth all things. Beware of murmuring and refrain the tongue from backbiting, for there is no word so secret that shall go for nought, and the mouth that belieth, that slandereth a brother, a sister, the leadership, or the Lord, slayeth the soul. Many speak evil against leadership because they do not like when judgment comes out; a problem with the leadership the Most High set up is a problem with the Most High Himself.

The people cried unto Moses, and when Moses prayed unto the Lord, the fire was quenched; the Most High quenched the fire because Moses prayed on behalf of the children of Israel. The place was called Taberah, because the fire of the Lord burnt among them.

The mixed multitude that fell a lusting were the other nations sprinkled in among Israel, the mixed multitude that went up with the people out of Egypt; the law in Leviticus tells what they were for, to be the bondmen and bondmaids of Israel. It was not Israel complaining at first; it was the nations lusting after the food of Egypt, and the children of Israel, gullible and assimilated as always, followed right after them and murmured against their God. The same spirit is on the people now: whatever the other nations want to do, our people want to be part of it. They wept for the fish they ate freely in Egypt, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic, right after the Lord destroyed the Egyptians to bring them out of bondage. It is the same today with the entertainments and comforts of this captivity, and some will do the same thing again in the wilderness when the Most High brings the people back out. They had just seen the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp, and they went back and did the same thing. We are the same people today; there is nothing new under the sun, and these things were written aforetime for our learning, so we can read them and refuse to do as they did.

The manna was as coriander seed, the colour of bdellium; the people gathered it, ground it, baked it in pans, and the taste of it was as the taste of fresh oil. Read precept upon precept to understand what they despised: manna is angels' food, the food the Lord feeds the angels, sent from heaven prepared without their labour; they only had to pick it up. The manna was able to content every man's delight and agreed to every taste, tempering itself to every man's liking; whatever the tongue craved that day, the manna tasted like it. To complain about that provision, including the very garlic and onions and melons they wept for, was pure rebellion against the Lord God of heaven and earth.
Moses heard the people weep throughout their families, every man in the door of his tent; the anger of the Lord was kindled greatly, and Moses also was displeased.

Moses asked the Most High why He had afflicted His servant and laid the burden of all this people on him: have I conceived all this people, that thou shouldest say, Carry them in thy bosom as a nursing father? He was carrying grown people who acted like children. The people Moses bore are the same people today; this teaching identifies the children of Israel with the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native American Indians, and the sheer rebellion and complaining in these chapters is one of the marks of the people. Moses said, If thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand; he would rather die than bear so rebellious a people alone and look upon his own wretchedness.

The Lord told Moses to gather seventy men of the elders of Israel to the tabernacle, and He would take of the spirit upon Moses and put it upon them, that they bear the burden of the people with him. Leadership works the same way today. The spirit on the head, the willingness to put in work, the humility, the patience, is meant to trickle down to the men below him, and the spirit the lead sisters roll in sets the spirit of the sisters in the congregation. That is why the leaders must be right according to the scriptures, because the Most High takes their spirit and lets it come upon the others.

The Lord said, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow, and ye shall eat flesh; ye have wept in the ears of the Lord, saying, It was well with us in Egypt, therefore the Lord will give you flesh. Not one day, nor two, nor five, nor ten, nor twenty days, but a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils and it be loathsome unto you. He fed them so much of the flesh they begged for that they would grow sick of it and hate it. The reason for the judgment is stated plainly: because ye have despised the Lord which is among you. They spoke evil of His manna and wept to go back among the oppressors He had just destroyed.

Moses inquired how it could be done: the people are six hundred thousand footmen, and that count is not including women and children; there were millions in the wilderness. Shall the flocks and the herds be slain for them, or all the fish of the sea gathered together for them, to suffice them? The Lord answered, Is the LORD'S hand waxed short? The One who destroyed Egypt asks whether His hand is short; thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass unto thee or not. Be patient and watch the word come to pass.

Moses gathered the seventy elders round about the tabernacle, and the Lord came down in a cloud and took of the spirit that was upon Moses and gave it unto the seventy elders; and when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease. The same thing happened with Elijah and Elisha. Elisha, Elijah's right hand and disciple, asked for a double portion of his master's spirit before Elijah was taken up, and when the sons of the prophets saw Elisha smite Jordan with the mantle, they said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha. It was the same in the time of Christ: the apostles taught like Christ, and men could tell that spirit was on them, just as the elders carried the spirit of Moses.

Two of the men, Eldad and Medad, remained in the camp, and the spirit rested upon them, and they prophesied in the camp. A young man ran and told Moses, and Joshua the son of Nun said, My lord Moses, forbid them. Moses answered, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the LORD'S people were prophets. Joshua was carrying a spirit of envy, and Moses corrected it; the Most High wants all His people to be prophets. The same is a lesson today: do not envy the gift on another brother or sister, but glean from it. A brother may be a better teacher, a sister a better labourer; go and learn from them rather than rolling in envy, for the Lord would put His spirit upon them all.

A wind from the Lord brought quails from the sea and let them fall by the camp, a day's journey on this side and on the other, two cubits high upon the face of the earth, and the people gathered them. While the flesh was yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the wrath of the Lord was kindled and He smote the people with a very great plague, exactly as He had warned. The place was called Kibrothhattaavah, the graves of lust, because there they buried the people that lusted. The Most High had overfed them because they murmured, but the lesson also stands in nature: excess of meat brings sickness. Animal protein is good for the body, but it is a matter of moderation, not overindulgence.
